observations.repro_000: Both candidates keep lion focus but change fur/detail and boundary appearance; surrounding subjects have strong blur; A/B differences are modest at sampled frames.
observations.repro_001: Rabbit blur extent and shape vary relative to GT; foreground overlap/bird edges differ. Both candidates preserve broad focus direction, without isolated black-frame failure.
observations.repro_003: Focused bear/deer detail and contrast are regenerated; person remains blurred. Neither candidate is uniformly favored by the sampled appearance.
observations.repro_004: Weak-blur outputs remain near sharp input and often preserve more high-frequency background detail than GT; no gross decoding/channel error.
observations.repro_006: Weak-blur scene retains much sharper tree texture than GT in both candidates; preserve model behavior.
observations.repro_007: Both outputs sharpen/redraw cat and globe detail compared with GT; small people differ. No new rerun or strength correction.
observations.repro_008: Expected foreground goat blur is present, with differences in depth-edge mixing and texture.
observations.repro_012: Highest FD scene for both candidates; strong blur/background and dog/face appearance differ, B often more diffuse. No unique temporal cause inferred from five keyframes.
observations.repro_017: A sometimes keeps woman/dog/tiger areas sharper than GT; B changes blur response and reduces some mismatch but not uniformly across sampled times.
observations.repro_193: Lowest PSNR for both: background, kangaroo silhouette, monkey and person are substantially more blurred than GT; focused camel remains sharp. Black kangaroo is already in input, not a generated black-block bug.
observations.repro_197: Largest paired VideoMAE feature distance for both: background/people/far animals are over-smoothed relative to GT and have different silhouettes; focused small giraffe remains sharp.

decision.reason: Four metrics favor A in paper closeness, two favor B; no predeclared priority, no voting/weights/new candidate. Report A/B in Table V and leave main adapter under review.

scope: Review of existing complete-200 outputs; no model execution, metric changes or new parameter search. Five keyframes per clip cannot exclude unsampled flicker; paired feature distance is not per-video FVD.

post_review_reporting_selection.rationale: After the complete 200-scene metrics and qualitative review, the user selected the Normalized candidate for the main reproduction table. A is closer to the Any-to-Bokeh BokehDiff row on PSNR/SSIM/FD/RM, but the A/B gaps on those four metrics are relatively small; B is closer on FVD and VFID-I, with FVD 65.996926 versus paper 65.678 (absolute difference 0.318926).
post_review_reporting_selection.scope: Reporting/reproduction selection only. This does not establish that Any-to-Bokeh used the Normalized private adapter. Both complete candidates remain retained in Table V; no rerun, third candidate, K-scale search, metric weighting, or benchmark change.
